title: Invariant affine charts of an admissible finite-group scheme quotient
statement: Let $M$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let a finite group $H$ act on $M$ by scheme automorphisms. Assume the action is admissible, meaning that every orbit of underlying points is contained in an affine open subscheme. Then there is a categorical quotient $q:M\to Q$ in schemes. Categorical means that every $H$-invariant scheme morphism $M\to Z$ factors uniquely through $q$. The map $q$ is affine, integral and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], its topology is the orbit-space topology, and its geometric fibres are $H$-orbits. There is a covering of $M$ by $H$-stable affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ such that $q(W)$ is open affine, $q^{-1}q(W)=W$, and the restriction $W\to q(W)$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}(B^H)$, where $B^H=\{b\in B:h(b)=b\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. For every affine open $V\subseteq Q$, its inverse image is affine and $\mathcal O_Q(V)$ is the invariant subring of $\mathcal O_M(q^{-1}V)$ under the canonical map. Restriction to an invariant open of $M$ is its categorical quotient onto the corresponding open of $Q$. No finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis and no module-finiteness conclusion for $q$ are imposed.

source.place: Expose IX 1.4, printed pp.132--133, admissible scheme quotients used there. Affine local integrality and orbit fibres: Stacks groupoids.tex Tags 03BJ (lemma-integral-over-invariants) and 03BL (lemma-points), for the constant finite-group action groupoid; gluing the invariant affine charts is the admissible quotient assertion used in IX 1.4.

proof.text: If $M$ is empty, take $Q=\operatorname{Spec}0$ and the unique map; every assertion follows directly (all point sets and all nonempty affine charts are absent). Henceforth consider a point $x$ and its nonempty finite orbit $E=Hx$. More generally let $O$ be any invariant open containing $E$. Admissibility supplies an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $E$. Set $T=O\cap\bigcap_{h\in H}hU$. This is an invariant open containing $E$ and contained in $U$. Write the closed subset $U\setminus T$ as $V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subset A$. Since none of the orbit primes belongs to $V(J)$, $J$ is contained in none of these finitely many prime ideals. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to choose $a\in J$ outside all of them. Then $E\subset A_0:=D_U(a)\subset T$, and $A_0$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Every translate $hA_0$ is affine and contained in $T\subset U$. The affine scheme $U$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] INSIDE $U$ shows that $W=\bigcap_{h\in H}hA_0$ is affine. It is invariant, contains $E$, and lies in $O$. Taking $O=M$ gives the required invariant affine covering; the stronger assertion also gives such a covering inside every invariant open. No intersection theorem is applied to $M$ itself.

source.place: Tag 00DS (lemma-silly, including its finite-set neighbourhood slogan); schemes.tex Tags 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), 01KN (lemma-affine-separated), 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated)

proof.text: For each invariant affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, give $B$ the left action $h\cdot b=(h^{-1})^*b$ and put $C=B^H$. For $b\in B$ the polynomial $P_b(t)=\prod_{h\in H}(t-h\cdot b)$ is monic, has coefficients in $C$ because the action permutes its factors, and vanishes at $b$ because the identity factor vanishes. Thus $C\hookrightarrow B$ is integral. This direct finite-product argument proves the specialization of Tag 03BJ that we need; it does not claim that $B$ is a finite $C$-module.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (lemma-integral-over-invariants), constant finite-group specialization of its norm polynomial

proof.text: On $W$, form the action groupoid with arrow scheme $R=\coprod_{h\in H}W$, source $s(h,w)=w$, target $t(h,w)=hw$, identity $(1,w)$, inversion $(h,w)\mapsto(h^{-1},hw)$, and composition $(g,hw)\circ(h,w)=(gh,w)$. The group laws verify all the groupoid identities on every test scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $R=\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_H B)$ is affine. Both $s$ and $t$ are finite: on each summand they are isomorphisms, hence finite, and induction on the nonempty finite set $H$ applies [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct]. They are also etale by [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale], since the summand maps are isomorphisms. Isomorphisms are finite and etale directly: their affine coordinate maps are ring isomorphisms, so are generated by $1$ as modules, are flat and finitely presented, and their diagonals are isomorphisms. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] etaleness supplies flatness and local finite presentation; together with finiteness this is precisely finite local freeness [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The equalizer of $s^\sharp,t^\sharp:B\rightrightarrows\prod_HB$ is $C$, because its component equations say $h^*b=b$ for every $h$.

source.place: Tag 03BL (lemma-points), application to the constant action groupoid; morphisms.tex Tag 0CYI (lemma-finite-union-finite) and Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize)

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] to the affine groupoid just checked. The map $p_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ induced by $C\hookrightarrow B$ is surjective, and two underlying points have the same image exactly when they are in one $H$-orbit: an arrow of $R$ is a point of a summand indexed by $h$. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$, the map $W(\Omega)\to(\operatorname{Spec}C)(\Omega)$ is surjective with fibres precisely the $H$-orbits. The relation generated by arrows is already the orbit relation, by identity, inverse, and multiplication. Moreover $p_W$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map], since Step 2 proves integrality. A continuous closed surjection has quotient topology: if $p_W^{-1}(F)$ is closed, then $F=p_W(p_W^{-1}(F))$ is closed. Thus the canonical bijection $|W|/H\to|\operatorname{Spec}C|$ is a homeomorphism.

For the same $B,C$ and any $f\in C$, the canonical map $C_f\to(B_f)^H$ is an isomorphism. It is injective: $c/f^n=0$ in $B_f$ means $f^rc=0$ in $B$ for some $r$, and this equality already holds in the subring $C$. For surjectivity write an invariant element as $b/f^n$. For every $h$ its invariance means $f^{r_h}(h\cdot b-b)=0$ for some $r_h$. Since $H$ is finite, choose $r\geq r_h$ for all $h$. Then $f^rb\in C$, and $b/f^n=(f^rb)/f^{n+r}$ is in the image. These isomorphisms are induced by the inclusions of subrings and the localization maps, so commute with restriction to smaller basic opens. This is an explicit common-denominator argument, valid even when $f$ is a zero divisor.

source.place: Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), (3) for localization; here proved directly for finite-group invariants

proof.text: Construct $|Q|$ as the set of $H$-orbits in $|M|$, with the quotient topology, and let $q$ be the orbit projection. It is open: for every open $A\subset M$, $q^{-1}q(A)=\bigcup_{h\in H}hA$ is open. Invariant opens $A$ correspond bijectively to opens $q(A)$, with $q^{-1}q(A)=A$. On an open $V\subset Q$ define $\mathcal O_Q(V)=\mathcal O_M(q^{-1}V)^H$, with the inherited restriction maps. This is a sheaf of rings: sections that agree on a cover glue uniquely in $\mathcal O_M$, and every translate of the glued section has the same restrictions as that section, so uniqueness makes it invariant. Inclusion of invariant sections defines a map of sheaves $\mathcal O_Q\to q_*\mathcal O_M$. This specifies the entire ringed space and map; no scheme quotient or gluing theorem is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0091 (definition-ringed-space), with the explicit orbit-space invariant-sheaf construction for the admissible quotient used in ILO IX 1.4

proof.text: For an invariant affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $q(W)$ is open, $q^{-1}q(W)=W$, and the subspace quotient topology on $q(W)$ is $|W|/H$ (the restriction of the open quotient projection to a saturated open is again an open quotient projection). Identify this space with $|\operatorname{Spec}C|$ by Step 4. The inverse image of a basic open $D_C(f)$ is $D_B(f)$, since contraction of a prime contains $f$ exactly when the prime contains its image. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], the structure sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}C$ has sections $C_f$ on $D_C(f)$, while the sheaf just constructed on $q(W)$ has sections $(B_f)^H$. Step 5 identifies these, compatibly with restrictions. Basic opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. Therefore these identifications give a sheaf isomorphism on all opens: cover an open by its basic opens, and glue the compatible local images; uniqueness of gluing gives the inverse. Hence $q(W)$ with its constructed sheaf is canonically the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(B^H)$.

These affine opens $q(W)$ cover $Q$, so every stalk of $\mathcal O_Q$ is local and $(Q,\mathcal O_Q)$ is locally affine, hence a scheme (the defining local condition of Stacks Tag 01IJ, the notion [def-pc-scheme]). On each $W$, the map of ringed spaces constructed in Step 6 is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\hookrightarrow B)$: on a basic open its section map is exactly $C_f\to B_f$. This is a scheme morphism by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so its stalk maps are local. Every point of $M$ lies in such a $W$; hence all stalk maps of $q$ are local. Thus $q$ is a scheme morphism by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], with the claimed canonical affine restrictions. Step 4 gives its geometric point fibres, since the preimage of any $q(W)$ is exactly $W$.

The affine covering $\{q(W)\}$ has affine inverse images $W$. Therefore [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] proves $q$ affine. In particular, for EVERY affine open $V\subset Q$, $q^{-1}V$ is affine. By the actual definition of $\mathcal O_Q$ in Step 6, the canonical section map identifies $\mathcal O_Q(V)$ with $\mathcal O_M(q^{-1}V)^H$. Apply the monic orbit polynomial of Step 2 to this latter affine ring and its $H$-action. It shows that the section ring of $q^{-1}V$ is integral over $\mathcal O_Q(V)$. Since this works for every affine $V$, [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] proves $q$ integral. Surjectivity and the orbit-space topology are already part of its construction. This argument imposes no finiteness-of-generation assumption on any of these rings.

source.place: Tag 01S8 (lemma-characterize-affine) and Tag 01WH (definition-integral); groupoids.tex Tag 03BJ orbit polynomial

proof.text: Let $u:M\to Z$ be an $H$-invariant scheme morphism. Its underlying map factors uniquely as $v\circ q$ on orbit sets; $v$ is continuous by the quotient topology. For every open $A\subset Z$, $u^\sharp$ takes values in the invariant sections on $u^{-1}A=q^{-1}v^{-1}A$, because $u\circ h=u$ as scheme morphisms. Thus it factors through $\mathcal O_Q(v^{-1}A)$, giving a map of sheaves $v^\sharp$. This ringed-space morphism is local on stalks: for $y\in Q$ choose $x\in M$ over $y$. The composite $\mathcal O_{Z,v(y)}\to\mathcal O_{Q,y}\to\mathcal O_{M,x}$ is $u_x^\sharp$. If $a$ is in the maximal ideal of the first ring and its image in $\mathcal O_{Q,y}$ were a unit, its image in $\mathcal O_{M,x}$ would be a unit, contradicting locality of $u_x^\sharp$. Consequently $v$ is a scheme morphism by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Uniqueness of its sheaf map follows because every $\mathcal O_Q(V)\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_M(q^{-1}V)$ is injective. This proves exactly the categorical universal property, including arbitrary nonseparated targets $Z$.

source.place: Tag 01HB (definition-locally-ringed-space), applied directly to the invariant-sheaf construction; ILO IX 1.4 categorical admissible quotient

proof.text: If $A\subset M$ is invariant open, $B=q(A)$ is open and $q^{-1}B=A$. The restriction of the quotient topology to $B$ is the orbit quotient of $A$, and for every open $V\subset B$ the restricted structure sheaf is still $\mathcal O_A((q|_A)^{-1}V)^H$. Apply the explicit factorization argument of Step 10 with $A,B$ in place of $M,Q$; surjectivity and injectivity of the invariant-section inclusions hold for the restrictions as well. It proves that $A\to B$ is the categorical quotient of $A$. This completes the restriction assertion without any assumption that $A$ is affine or quasi-compact.

tool_uses.why: Finite prime avoidance gives one basic affine neighbourhood of a finite orbit inside a prescribed open; the perverse unit contains no such algebra tool.
Basic-open affineness and section localization supply actual affine neighbourhoods and the invariant sheaf chart comparison.
Separatedness is used only for the ambient affine U, never for M.
Generic affine intersection lemma, applied inside the affine U to the finitely many translated smaller affine opens.
Finite affine coproduct formula makes the action arrow scheme affine.
Generic finiteness under binary coproduct, iterated to check the action groupoid hypotheses.
Generic etale coproduct theorem checks flatness and local finite presentation of the action arrows.
Generic 03BL orbit-fibre theorem gives ordinary and geometric orbit fibres of each affine invariant spectrum.
Generic closedness of integral spectrum maps identifies the affine spectrum topology with the orbit quotient topology.
Generic basic-open basis is used in the sheaf comparison, not a replacement of any perverse-unit step.
Generic target-local criterion upgrades the explicit quotient charts to affineness over every affine open.

The statement is byte-identical to the base (checked against the Q138 snapshot). The only stmt_deps change adds def-weil-affine-spectrum, which the statement uses for Spec. There are no new nodes. Step 1: prime avoidance (00DS) is applied to J with V(J)=U minus T, where T=O ∩ (intersection of the hU), so D_U(a) lies in T. The finite intersection of the affine opens hA0 is affine by 01KP inside the affine U, never inside M. Step 2: the coefficients of the orbit polynomial are invariant, so B is integral over B^H; module-finiteness is not claimed. Step 3: the action groupoid is the coproduct of copies of W, which is Spec of the product of copies of B. s and t are finite (0CYI, by induction) and étale (coproduct node), hence finite locally free, and their equalizer is B^H. So 03BL applies. Step 4: the fibres are orbits, both on points and on geometric points. Integral implies closed (00GU/00HZ), which gives the quotient topology. Step 5: C_f is isomorphic to (B_f)^H by a common exponent; this holds for zero-divisor f and needs no division by |H|. Steps 6-8: the invariant sheaf is a sheaf; on the basis of basic opens it matches Spec C via 01I3/00E0; and the stalk maps are local. Step 9: q is affine by 01S8, and O_Q(V)=O_M(q^{-1}V)^H for every affine V, so q is integral (01WH). Steps 10-11: the universal property holds, with locality checked through u_x^sharp and uniqueness from injectivity on sections. It works for nonseparated targets and restricts to invariant opens. No cycle (the item is not in its own 370-node closure). There is no duplicate in the DAG: lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient is Noetherian, tame and finite; def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient is a definition; the lem-a1 groupoid tools are affine only.
